title: The Equipotential Explorer
summary: Find points that share a potential, read the field from the potential between two probes and rank fields by band spacing.
subject: physics
concepts: The field is perpendicular to an equipotential
Field strength from the spacing of equipotentials
learningOutcome: The student can find points of equal potential, say how the field meets an equipotential surface, find a uniform field from a potential difference, and compare fields from equipotential spacing.

levels.title: Find the equipotential
levels.adds: Baseline: an equipotential joins points of equal potential, and the field meets it at right angles (Ex 2.3).
hints: The potential is kq/r summed over the charges. Points with the same total are on the same equipotential.
Halfway between two equal and opposite charges the potential is zero along a whole plane.
The field is perpendicular to the surface: otherwise moving along it would cost energy.

levels.title: Field from potential
levels.adds: New idea: in a uniform field E = ΔV/d, pointing towards lower potential.
hints: ΔV is the difference of the two readings; d is their separation along the field, in metres.
The field points from the higher potential to the lower.

levels.title: Rank by crowding
levels.adds: New idea: E = −dV/dr, so closely spaced equipotentials mean a strong field.
hints: Each colour step is an equipotential surface with a fixed potential difference to the next.
The closer the steps, the larger the change of V per metre.
Near a charge the bands crowd together.

misconceptions: The field points along an equipotential surface
The potential is zero only at the midpoint between opposite charges, not on a whole plane
The field points towards higher potential
